Overview

Nightscout xDrip is a multi-module Android data hub and processor for glucose, treatment, insulin, activity, and device data. The README documents support for numerous CGMs, glucose meters, pumps, insulin pens, watches, follower phones, Nightscout, Tidepool, MongoDB, InfluxDB, AndroidAPS, and other companion apps. The repository is primarily an Android phone application with a separate Wear OS application and reusable integration modules.

Core components

  • Android application shell and UI — app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip
    Activities, services, receivers, widgets, preferences, notifications, and web-service endpoints form the main Android entry surface. app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml defines the platform-facing component boundary.
  • Domain models and local persistence — app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/models
    Domain records include glucose readings, calibrations, sensors, treatments, insulin, profiles, alerts, and device state. Database-facing tables are organized under app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/tables; schema migrations are stored in app/src/main/assets/migrations. Preferences and key/value state are separately represented under app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/store and app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/utilitymodels.
  • Device acquisition and protocol adapters — app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/services
    Collection services and protocol packages cover Dexcom/G5/G6/G7, Libre, Medtrum, glucose meters, NFC, USB, and other Bluetooth devices. Supporting wire formats and protocol state are organized in cgm, g5model, glucosemeter, nfc, and importedlibraries.
  • Processing, calibration, alerts, and therapy logic — app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/calibrations
    Calibration implementations, smoothing/filtering, glucose-quality evaluators, predictive behavior, alert polling, insulin curves, and treatment calculations are separated into the calibration, processing, evaluators, alert, and insulin packages.
  • Cloud, follower, upload, and local-network interfaces — app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/cloud
    This area contains backup, peer/cloud messaging, and NightLite functionality. Related packages implement CareLink, Nightscout, Dexcom Share, web-follow, deposit, Tidepool, InfluxDB, Nocturne, and local web services. These are alternative external integrations rather than one mandatory backend.
  • Wear companion — wear/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip
    The Wear module provides watch activities, watch faces, alerts, charts, collection services, persistent records, and phone synchronization. It contains overlapping domain and protocol code so supported watches can display or collect data independently where documented.
  • Extension and integration modules — ipluginda/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/plugin
    Separate modules provide a plugin interface, Locale/Tasker API support, GluPro BLE support, and Keks protocol code. These are optional integration boundaries, distinct from the main application path.

Relationships

Android lifecycle components expose the app to users and platform events, while acquisition services and external-follow clients provide incoming device or network data. Models and table/state packages own the durable representation of that data. Processing and calibration packages provide domain transformations used by presentation, alerts, and uploads. Cloud, web, broadcast, Tasker, and plugin packages expose selected data or commands to external actors. The Wear application is a companion consumer/producer connected through the repository’s wear-integration and message areas; exact call order is not established by the tree alone.

Public entry points and boundaries

Runtime entry points are Android manifest-declared activities, services, broadcast receivers, content/web-service components, widgets, and Wear components. External actors include CGM meters and pumps, companion apps, watches, Nightscout/Tidepool/cloud servers, and user automation tools. Configuration, credentials, permissions, and device availability are application/deployment inputs; this repository owns the adapters and processing implementations but not those external systems.
